_doc: Named channels. A preset is a list of paths; a path has a delay (ms, relative to the first) and one or more components: Rayleigh scatter (power, spread_hz = 2 sigma of its Gaussian Doppler spectrum, shift_hz) or specular (a steady ray: power, shift_hz). Shorthand: a path with power/spread_hz/shift_hz is one scatter component. Path powers of a preset add up to 1. Checked against the ITU-R texts on 2026-11-23.

flat-slow.source: ITU-R F.520-2 §2.1: flat fading, one path, 0.2 Hz

flat-fast.source: ITU-R F.520-2 §2.1: flat fading, one path, 1 Hz

poor.source: ITU-R F.520-2 §2.2.3 (= F.1487 mid-latitude disturbed; MIL-STD-188-110 and codec2 'MPP' use the same)

mid-nvis-disturbed.source: ITU-R F.1487 Annex 3 §3.4 (a ground wave may be added)

polar-cap-14mhz.source: Stocker, Warrington & Siddle 2013, Radio Science 48:638, Table 2: 95th percentiles 2009-2012, Qaanaaq-Ny-Alesund (polar cap, 1705 km), winter day, 14.36 MHz; Doppler spread there is the 80 %-power width (13.0 Hz), here 2 sigma = width / 1.2816; multipath spread (first mode to last, modes within 12 dB) is the path delay

polar-cap-5mhz.source: Stocker, Warrington & Siddle 2013, Radio Science 48:638, Table 2: 95th percentiles 2009-2012, Qaanaaq-Ny-Alesund (polar cap, 1705 km), winter day, 4.64 MHz; Doppler spread there is the 80 %-power width (3.5 Hz), here 2 sigma = width / 1.2816; multipath spread (first mode to last, modes within 12 dB) is the path delay

trough-5mhz.source: Stocker, Warrington & Siddle 2013, Radio Science 48:638, Table 2: 95th percentiles 2009-2012, Nurmijarvi-Bruntingthorpe (mid-latitude trough, 1800 km), winter day, 4.64 MHz; Doppler spread there is the 80 %-power width (1.5 Hz), here 2 sigma = width / 1.2816; multipath spread (first mode to last, modes within 12 dB) is the path delay

auroral-7-11mhz.source: Angling et al. 1998, Radio Science 33:97, Table 5 (DAMSON, SNR -5 to 5 dB, no guard, 0000-2400 UT): values exceeded 5 % of the time on Harstad-Kiruna (194 km, auroral zone), 6.7-11.2 MHz band, read separately from the 5 % contour, not as a joint pair; Doppler spread there is the 80 %-power width (30.3 Hz), here 2 sigma = width / 1.2816 (the paper's own factor 0.78); multipath spread (10.7 ms) is the path delay

auroral-14-22mhz.source: Angling et al. 1998, Radio Science 33:97, Table 5 (DAMSON, SNR -5 to 5 dB, no guard, 0000-2400 UT): values exceeded 5 % of the time on Harstad-Kiruna (194 km, auroral zone), 14.4-21.9 MHz band, read separately from the 5 % contour, not as a joint pair; Doppler spread there is the 80 %-power width (54.6 Hz), here 2 sigma = width / 1.2816 (the paper's own factor 0.78); multipath spread (5.1 ms) is the path delay

equatorial-spread-f.source: Fitzgerald, Argo & Carlos 1999, Radio Science 34:167 (Maloelap-Bikini, 700 km, 10.2 MHz, Aug 1990): spread 2 sigma of a Gaussian whose -10 dB width is the median 6 Hz (the -30 dB pedestal, median 15 Hz, is not modelled); delay from the coherence bandwidth (50 % coherence) that 75 % of evenings were below, 1.5 kHz, as |cos(pi df tau)| = 0.5

nvis-java-7mhz.source: Dear et al. 2024, Radio Science 59:e2023RS007877 (Pameungpeuk-Bandung NVIS, 7 MHz, Dec 2021, quiet): delay = 2 x the mean rms delay spread 0.4627 ms (two equal paths have rms delay tau/2), shift the mean Doppler 0.9 Hz; no Doppler spread given, so 0.5 Hz from F.1487 Annex 3 low-latitude quiet

high-latitude-wb-median.source: Nissen & Bello 1994, MITRE MP 94B0000006 (DTIC ADA277877; Sondrestrom-Bedford, 3100 km, Mar-Apr 1992, 1 MHz probe): rms (2 sigma) spreads; 50th percentile: Doppler spread 5 Hz, delay spread 100 us (= the path delay for two equal paths), Doppler shift magnitude 0.5 Hz; percentiles taken separately

high-latitude-wb-90.source: Nissen & Bello 1994, MITRE MP 94B0000006 (DTIC ADA277877; Sondrestrom-Bedford, 3100 km, Mar-Apr 1992, 1 MHz probe): rms (2 sigma) spreads; 90th percentile: Doppler spread 13 Hz, delay spread 400 ("slightly larger") us (= the path delay for two equal paths), Doppler shift magnitude 3 ("just below") Hz; percentiles taken separately
